chunks: My father (rah) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to us from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Muhammad ibn Hamran from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever says 'La ilaha illallah' with sincerity will enter Paradise, and his sincerity with it is that 'La ilaha illallah' keeps him away from what Allah has prohibited.

key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: There is no god but Allah (declaration of monotheism)

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of sincerity (ikhlas) in reciting La ilaha illallah according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights that true *ikhlas* in the Shahada is evidenced by its practical function as a restraining force against sin, a concept central to Shia understanding of the unity of knowledge and action. This hadith bridges the theological declaration of monotheism with ethical conduct, emphasizing that verbal testimony must manifest in behavioral discipline to secure salvation.
